findings.problem: `ex` and `ey` are two ~15-line proofs with the same structure. Each does `Lp.ext`, then `filter_upwards` over the same eight a.e. facts (toLp coercion, Lp.coeFn_sub/add, two Lp.coeFn_smul, two angularCircleAction_coe, two quasi-measure-preserving transports of coeFn_toLp), then `rw [h0,…,h5]`, then `change`, then `rw [h6, h7, x/yDerivative_rotate]`. Only sub/add, the coefficient pair and the final pointwise rotate lemma differ. The a.e. bookkeeping is the mathematical content here, and it is written out twice. It is also fragile, since a change to the h-numbering must be made in both copies.
findings.proposed_change: Prove the identification once, in a form that avoids a.e. reasoning. First prove a rotation-transport lemma: for hg : MemLp g 2 (doubleMeasure Q), `(angularCircleAction Q).act θ (hg.toLp g) = (hg.comp_measurePreserving (measurePreserving_doubleRotate Q θ.toCircle)).toLp (g ∘ doubleRotate θ.toCircle)`. This is the existing `circleAction_toLp`, so it is already available. Then state one lemma along the lines of `rotate_combo_toLp (Q) (θ) (p q : ℂ) (hx hy) (hc : MemLp (p • (xDerivative f ∘ doubleRotate a) + q • (yDerivative f ∘ doubleRotate a)) 2 _) : hc.toLp _ = p • act θ (hx.toLp _) + q • act θ (hy.toLp _)`. Prove it by rewriting with `circleAction_toLp` and then `MemLp.toLp_add` and `MemLp.toLp_const_smul` (or one `Lp.ext` with a single `filter_upwards`). Take the subtraction case as `q := -im`. Both `ex` and `ey` then follow from this lemma and `funext (xDerivative_rotate a f)` / `funext (yDerivative_rotate a f)`, in a couple of lines each.
findings.benefit: This removes about 30 lines of duplicated, hard-to-read a.e. bookkeeping and gives the identification a named statement. `seam_rotated_generators` is then reduced to applying the two seam generator lemmas and rewriting, which is easier to maintain and review.

findings.problem: The two lemmas have byte-identical proofs: the same `by_cases hb` chain, the same `simp only` list, `apply Complex.ext`, a global `simp … at *`, and the same two-term `nlinarith` hint using the circle relation. Only the statement differs. This is a rotation-matrix identity (the vector v is recovered from the rotated vector and its transverse), proved by case analysis plus nonlinear arithmetic, and it is written twice. Downstream, `xDerivative_rotate`/`yDerivative_rotate` and `rotate_x_memLp`/`rotate_y_memLp` also repeat their shared skeleton: change to `fderiv`, rewrite with the decomposition, `map_*`/`map_smul`, `rfl`, and `MemLp.comp_measurePreserving` + `const_smul` + `sub`/`add`. The `simp … at *` and `nlinarith` calls are brittle, so a fix to one proof has to be repeated in the other.
findings.proposed_change: Factor out the algebra once. Introduce `w := ((if b = 0 then a else a⁻¹) * v : Circle)` and prove a single lemma that gives the transverse-of-rotated formula, e.g. `transverseVelocity w b = (-a.im) • v' + a.re • transverseVelocity v b`-style, or a lemma stating that `(v, transverseVelocity v b)` is obtained from `(w, transverseVelocity w b)` by the rotation matrix of `a`. Then derive the second identity by one `linear_combination` or by rewriting the first. This needs only one `by_cases` and one `nlinarith` block. For the MemLp lemmas, state a single `rotate_comb_memLp` for `p • (xDerivative f ∘ doubleRotate a) + q • (yDerivative f ∘ doubleRotate a)` and obtain both lemmas by specialising `q` to `-im` and `p`/`q` to `im`/`re`. The same lemma serves the combination lemma proposed for `ex`/`ey` above.
findings.benefit: The rotation algebra and its nlinarith certificate are written once, and the x/y asymmetry is limited to the choice of coefficients. This shortens the file, removes copy-paste risk and makes the covariance computation easier to follow.
